text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday.

- Monday marks the ending of the first stage of the subregional agreement on arms control between Croatia and Yugoslavia. A Croatian team to inspect if Yugoslavia is holding its part of the bargain by cutting arms 40 percent.
- A final budget proposal envisages increased financing for the Education and Sports, Science and Technology Ministries as well as an additional 90 million kuna aid for new mothers.
- Stock market: Stock prices lower on average, but flat or higher at close last week.
- Parents who neglect their children are to lose custody of them according to a new draft law on family relations.
- The deputy parliament speaker, Vladimir Seks, denies rumours he is preparing changes to the constitution.
- Charity event "Everyone for the Children of Croatia" managed to raise some 5.6 million kuna over the weekend.

- A sealiner that slammed into the New Orleans shopping area due to a mechanical fault on Saturday, injuring 111 people, is a twin ship of a vessel owned by the Atlantska Plovidba shipping company headquartered in Dubrovnik.

- Some 5.0 million German marks necessary to found a new bank which would back fishermen and farmers. Most funds to be provided by HBOR (Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development). -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
